open_points.subject: service invocation request and response port metadata
open_points.text: “ManifestOperation M10 crosses from `module:bindings` to `module:service_invoker`” and “`capability:bindings.check_binding_current` returns the current ManifestOperation …; `capability:service_invoker.prepare_request` … places the inputs”
open_points.question: How does `service_invoker` receive the accepted OperationBinding M11 input and output ports needed to build multipart/query/body requests and validate response outputs, given that ManifestOperation M10 does not contain those ports?
options: `effects` reads the binding with `bindings.read_binding` and passes it with the ManifestOperation
`bindings.check_binding_current` returns both the binding and the current ManifestOperation
another capability supplies an invocation view containing both sets of facts
open_points.default_guess: Have `bindings.check_binding_current` return the accepted binding together with the current ManifestOperation.

open_points.subject: runtime source-port and target-port validation
open_points.text: “On success it validates each output against the source port, then against each target port before delivery”
open_points.question: Which capability supplies `runs` with the contract or binding port declarations needed for source-port and target-port validation, readiness, cardinality and mapping, especially for operation nodes when `runs` has no binding-read capability and FlowVersion stores only `binding_id`?
options: `runs` reads function contracts directly and obtains operation port declarations through a new `effects` capability
`flows.read_flow_version` returns an enriched immutable runtime graph containing all resolved ports
`runs` is allowed to read bindings directly in addition to its stated dependencies
open_points.default_guess: Make `flows.read_flow_version` return an enriched runtime graph containing the immutable resolved port declarations.
